module.title: Software Architecture Patterns And Engineering Design
module.description: Learn how professional engineers structure scalable codebases, separate responsibilities, manage complexity, and design maintainable production systems.

lessons.title: Why Software Architecture Matters

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Software architecture defines how applications are structured, organized, and designed for scalability and maintainability.

sections.heading: Codebases Become Massive
sections.content: Production applications can contain thousands of files, APIs, components, services, and workflows.

sections.heading: Bad Structure Creates Chaos
sections.content: Poorly organized systems become difficult to scale, debug, and maintain.

sections.heading: Architecture Organizes Complexity
sections.content: Professional systems separate responsibilities and define clear boundaries.

sections.heading: Engineering Requires System Design Thinking
sections.content: Senior engineers think about maintainability, scalability, and long-term development.

easyExample.title: City Planning Example
easyExample.content: Cities require organized roads, zones, utilities, and infrastructure instead of random construction.

summary: Professional engineering focuses heavily on scalable organization

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Clean architecture separates business logic from frameworks, databases, and external systems.

sections.heading: Business Logic Should Stay Independent
sections.content: Core application logic should not depend directly on frameworks or databases.

sections.heading: Layered System Design
sections.content: Applications separate controllers, services, repositories, and infrastructure.

sections.heading: Improved Flexibility
sections.content: Systems become easier to test, scale, and replace.

sections.heading: Professional Engineering Patterns
sections.content: Large production systems often rely heavily on layered architecture.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Kitchen Example
easyExample.content: Cooking recipes stay consistent even if kitchen equipment changes.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: The repository pattern separates database access logic from application business logic.

sections.heading: Direct Database Access Creates Coupling
sections.content: Mixing database queries everywhere creates difficult-to-maintain systems.

sections.heading: Repositories Centralize Data Access
sections.content: Applications organize database operations into dedicated repository layers.

sections.heading: Improved Scalability And Testing
sections.content: Repositories simplify updates, testing, and infrastructure changes.

sections.heading: Production Engineering Patterns
sections.content: Large systems often isolate storage infrastructure carefully.

easyExample.title: Library Desk Example
easyExample.content: People request books through librarians instead of directly accessing storage rooms.

lessons.title: Dependency Injection

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Dependency injection provides systems with required dependencies instead of creating them directly.

sections.heading: Hardcoded Dependencies Create Problems
sections.content: Applications become difficult to test and modify when systems directly create dependencies.

sections.heading: Dependency Injection Improves Flexibility
sections.content: Systems receive dependencies externally instead of tightly controlling everything internally.

sections.heading: Scalable Engineering Design
sections.content: Large applications use dependency injection heavily for maintainability.

sections.heading: Professional Architecture Thinking
sections.content: Modern engineering prioritizes modularity and loosely coupled systems.

easyExample.title: Electric Appliance Example
easyExample.content: Devices use standardized power outlets instead of requiring custom power systems.

summary: Large applications depend heavily on dependency management

lessons.title: Event Sourcing And CQRS Basics

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Event sourcing stores changes as events while CQRS separates read and write operations.

sections.heading: Traditional CRUD Systems Have Limits
sections.content: Large applications sometimes require specialized architectures for scalability and auditing.

sections.heading: Event Sourcing Stores History
sections.content: Systems record every state change as an event instead of storing only current values.

sections.heading: CQRS Separates Reads And Writes
sections.content: Applications optimize reading and writing operations independently.

sections.heading: Enterprise Engineering Patterns
sections.content: Large-scale financial, analytics, and distributed systems often use these patterns.

easyExample.title: Bank Transaction History Example
easyExample.content: Banks store every transaction event instead of only current account balances.

summary: Enterprise infrastructure often uses event-driven patterns

lessons.title: Production Architecture Engineering Thinking

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Production architecture engineering focuses on designing scalable, maintainable, modular systems capable of evolving over long-term growth.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Become Massive Ecosystems
sections.content: Production systems combine APIs, databases, AI systems, queues, infrastructure, frontend platforms, monitoring systems, and distributed services together.

sections.heading: Architecture Decisions Affect Everything
sections.content: Poor architecture creates scaling problems, technical debt, maintenance chaos, and operational instability.

sections.heading: Professional Engineering Prioritizes Long-Term Maintainability
sections.content: Large companies invest heavily in architecture planning and modular infrastructure design.

sections.heading: Thinking Beyond Features
sections.content: Professional engineers think about system evolution, scalability, separation of concerns, maintainability, and operational complexity.

easyExample.title: Modern Smart Factory Example
easyExample.content: Large factories organize robotics, logistics, manufacturing, monitoring, and automation systems into coordinated architectures.

basicCode.title: Production Architecture Flow
basicCode.code: Frontend → API Gateway → Services → Repositories → Databases → Event Systems → Monitoring

summary: Clean modular systems improve engineering workflows
Production infrastructure depends on strong architectural decisions
